findings: Old point and descriptor allocations are released before validation/allocation; old counts are reset.
Two allocations copy point records and distribute interior point references into descriptors; jitter amplitudes initialize to0. Descriptor last-point duration is replaced by resource word36.
Second allocation failure retains the first point allocation and count; cleanup/resource lifetime is required later.
limits: Physical allocation/free and memcpy are controlled transport primitives. Valid descriptor starts/count1/2/0/-1 and16 null/zero input guards only; out-of-range spans and invalid-start fault behavior, shared interior-reference resolution, Rust resource producer/teardown and whole manager/frame integration remain required.
